Evaluating an LLM on a full benchmark is costly, so we run it on n ≪ N items and predict its full score. # Venue: NeurIPS 2026, Main Track

Edition: NeurIPS 2026 (40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems), Main Track. Requirements from the world's venue library (`ht-role venue neurips`, retrieved 2026-11-14 from the sources cited per line); a few lines re-checked on 2026-11-26 against the OpenReview submission form and the reviewer guidelines. The paper is written to these requirements and reviewed against the standard in §Reviewers. Where the task's objective asks for something the venue says nothing about, the objective governs and the line says so.

## Choice (the objective lets the study pick ICML, ICLR or NeurIPS)

Chosen: **NeurIPS 2026**, because (1) it is the newest NeurIPS edition with a published call and style kit (the 2027 call returns HTTP 404, https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2027/CallForPapers, 2026-11-14), so "the newest edition of the chosen conference" is determinate; (2) the objective names the NeurIPS paper checklist as its example of the required checklist, and NeurIPS has the only mandatory question-by-question checklist of the three (ICML 2027: impact statement and AI-use statement; ICLR 2027: AI-use statement); (3) its requirements are completely established, whereas for ICML 2027 the submission form is not open and two official sources disagree on the file-size limit (50 MB vs 10 MB), and for ICLR 2027 the review-form scales could not be established (login wall) and the edition is already under review; (4) its reviewing criteria (quality, clarity, significance, originality) and the explicit statement that evaluating existing methods is as valuable as a new method (§Reviewers) fit a controlled comparison with a conditional or negative answer. Not a quality ranking of the venues. Caveats: the NeurIPS 2026 deadlines have passed (full paper 2026-05-06 AOE), so this is a paper written to the venue's standard, not a live submission; re-check for NeurIPS 2027 before any real submission.

## Page limit and what counts

- Main text: **nine content pages including all figures and tables** (https://neurips.cc/Conferences/2026/MainTrackHandbook; `template/neurips_2026.tex` §1.1).
- Not counted: references, optional technical appendices, the mandatory checklist; the kit adds acknowledgments (`template/neurips_2026.tex`). No page limit on references, appendix or checklist (OpenReview submission form, `pdf` field).
- Penalty: "Papers that exceed the page limit will not be reviewed" (`template/neurips_2026.tex`); desk rejection possible (Handbook). Reviewers are told not to penalise going over by a few lines.
- Camera-ready gets one more content page (10). The accepted papers profiled in `accepted-papers.md` are camera-ready, so scale their counts by 9/10.
- Order in the one PDF: paper content, references, appendices, checklist (Handbook). The paper must stand alone without the appendix; "adding critical experiments that support the main claims to an appendix is inappropriate" (`template/neurips_2026.tex`, Appendix A).
- No "broader impacts" section is required; a discussion of negative societal impact may go anywhere but counts against the nine pages (Handbook).

## Layout as enforced by the style file (`neurips_2026.sty`, copied in `paper-repo` `paper/template/`)

| Item | Value | Source |

| Paper size | US Letter (612 × 792 pt) | `.sty` (`letterpaper`); `.tex` §5 |

I chose NeurIPS 2026 Main Track as the venue and recorded its requirements and the accepted-paper profile. The style kit is in `paper-repo`, and both requests to me are answered and closed.

- **Venue:** NeurIPS 2026 is the newest NeurIPS edition with a published call. The objective's example checklist is NeurIPS's, and its rules are fully documented. ICML 2027 has an unopened form and two conflicting file-size limits. ICLR 2027's review scores couldn't be established.
- **Requirements** (`venue.md`, with sources and a "not established" section):
  - The main text is 9 pages including figures and tables; references, appendix and checklist don't count.
  - Layout is one column, 5.5 × 9 in, Times 10 pt.
  - Fonts must be Type 1 or embedded TrueType.
  - Submissions are anonymous, and the 16-item checklist is mandatory.
  - Code goes in an anonymised ZIP of at most 100 MB.
  - I recorded what reviewers judge, including the contribution type.
- **Figure sizes** (also in `venue.md`): full width is 5.5 in, and side-by-side panels are about 2.65 in each. The venue sets no minimum for text inside figures, so my recommendation of at least 7 pt at placed width is labelled as mine, not a venue rule.
- **Accepted-paper profile** (`accepted-papers.md`, with `profile/` giving the method and sample list): I measured 14 NeurIPS 2024–25 papers on LLM evaluation and prediction-powered inference. The sample is purposive, not random, and these are 10-page camera-ready versions. A 15th paper was dropped because its PDF layout was anomalous. The paper from the task's starter list (item 6) is deliberately not in the sample.
  - Median 5 figures and 0 tables in the main text, 6 items together (range 2–9).
  - Abstract median 177 words.
  - Introduction about 770 words.
  - References median 54.
- **Budget for this paper:** target 6 main figures and tables, 7 at most. The outline's ten items don't fit, so the story owner has to cut.
- **Contribution type:** I advised `story-repo` to frame the paper as General rather than Negative Results, which has a high bar even if the headline turns out negative.
- **Delivered:**
  - **Style kit:** the official style, the checklist skeleton and a usage note are in `paper-repo` `dev` under `paper/template/`. It builds offline with `latexmk`.
  - **Other pushes:** `venue.md`, `accepted-papers.md` and `venue-artifacts.json` are on my `main`, mirrored as the wiki pages `Venue` and `Accepted-papers`. `venue-artifacts.json` uses the path names from `paper-repo`'s `CODEOWNERS`.
- **Requests and notes sent:** I answered and closed `venue-repo`#2 (figtab) and #3 (paper-repo). I opened `story-repo`#4 (budget and contribution type) and `experiment-repo`#4 (code, data and checklist items). My own commitment is `venue-repo`#4.
- **LLM-use flag:** this study was run by LLM agents. Checklist item 16 and the paper must say so plainly. I flagged this to `paper-repo` in `venue.md`.
- **Not a live submission:** the NeurIPS 2026 deadlines passed in May, so this is a paper written to the venue's standard.
